newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Around 250 pubs may not have a valid licence.
newsitem.headline: Around 250 pubs may not have a valid licence.

text.p: About 250 Irish pubs may not have a valid licence to sell alcohol, a parliamentary committee was told on Tuesday by solicitors from the Law Society and the Solicitors' Mutual Defence Fund.
These are pubs which originally were hotels with hotel licences to sell alcohol and which have long ceased to have bedrooms.

"They operate a public bar, believing they hold a publican's licence but in reality they have a building with no licence," solicitors Maeve Hayes and Tom Shaw told the Legislation and Security Committee.

Even an inspection of the licensing register may not show up this confusion, as in many cases solicitors have found that a hotel licence has been renewed in the courts for years as a publican's licence. Often the court register does not show whether a licence is for an hotel or a pub.
"This gives rise to enormous losses to people who buy what they perceive to be a premises with a publican's licence but which turns out to have no licence at all," they said.
It has also led to claims against solicitors but if the problem is discovered after six years, then any claim against the solicitor may be statute barred.

Solicitors Maeve Hayes and Tom Shaw suggested that the best way out of this confusion was for those who are operating pubs for ten years, but who only have fatally flawed hotel licences, to be given a publican's licence at the annual renewal of pub licences.
The Committee agreed to recommend this to the Minister for Justice.
